content: If you're going through hell, keep going.
author: Winston Churchill
sourceWork: Blood, Toil, Tears and Sweat (1940 Speeches)
story:
Exiled to the political wilderness during the 1930s while European leaders appeased tyranny, Churchill was summoned to lead Britain during its darkest hour in 1940. Facing relentless Blitz bombings and imminent invasion, his indomitable rhetoric and refusal to surrender became the rallying voice that preserved Western democracy.

Confronting the trials of his era, Winston Churchill recognized that adversity is the ultimate crucible of the human spirit. Rather than seeking an easy path free from friction, he urged seekers to welcome the struggle as the very forge that tempers courage and character.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
